overview: This joint resolution would overturn a temporary tax law passed by the Council of the District of Columbia, the city's local legislature, in December 2025. That D.C. measure, the Income and Franchise Tax Conformity and Revision Temporary Amendment Act of 2025, changed how D.C.'s income and business taxes line up with federal tax rules. Under the Home Rule Act, which lets D.C. govern itself, Congress keeps the power to block D.C. laws by passing a resolution of disapproval that the President signs. As of February 4, 2026, a Senate committee had approved the resolution and it was awaiting a vote by the full Senate.
for: Supporters say Congress has constitutional authority over the nation's capital and should step in when it believes local tax changes are unwise or out of step with federal tax policy.
against: Critics say overturning a tax decision made by D.C.'s elected council overrides local self-government for the district's residents, who have no voting representation in Congress.
